question: What is the primary purpose of emergency contraception?

options.A: To induce an early abortion of an established pregnancy
options.B: To prevent pregnancy after unprotected sexual intercourse
options.C: To provide long-term protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.D: To regulate chronic menstrual cycle irregularities permanently

explanation: Emergency contraception is explicitly designed to prevent fertilization or implantation after unprotected intercourse, rather than terminate an existing pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h1)

question: Why is emergency contraception classified as a back-up method rather than routine contraception?

options.A: It requires surgical insertion before every single menstrual cycle
options.B: It does not provide continuous protection for subsequent acts of intercourse
options.C: It causes permanent infertility when used as a primary method
options.D: It is completely ineffective if used more than once a year

explanation: These methods only address a specific instance of unprotected intercourse and offer no safeguard against future unprotected acts. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h1)

question: Within how many hours post-intercourse are most emergency contraceptive pills traditionally recommended for optimal effectiveness?
explanation: While some formulations work up to 120 hours, the traditional standard for optimal efficacy of levonorgestrel pills is within 72 hours. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h2)

question: A client presents to the clinic 90 hours after unprotected intercourse requesting emergency contraception. Which method remains a viable clinical option for her?
explanation: The copper IUD can be inserted up to 120 hours after unprotected intercourse, making it suitable for clients presenting past the 72-hour window for certain pills. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h2)

question: What is the primary mechanism of action of emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: Causing immediate shedding of the uterine lining
options.B: Killing sperm instantly upon contact in the vagina
options.C: Destroying fertilized ova in the fallopian tubes

explanation: Hormonal emergency contraceptives work by suppressing or pushing back the release of the oocyte so fertilization cannot occur. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h3)

question: What happens if emergency contraceptive pills are ingested after ovulation has already occurred in the current cycle?

options.A: They have little to no effect on preventing pregnancy from that act
options.B: They cause permanent cessation of future menstrual cycles
options.C: They immediately terminate the newly formed zygote
options.D: They induce heavy bleeding to flush out the egg

explanation: Because the mechanism relies on delaying ovulation, taking the pills after ovulation has already taken place renders them largely ineffective. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h3)

question: Which active ingredient is most commonly found in single-dose dedicated emergency contraceptive pills sold over-the-counter?
explanation: Levonorgestrel 1.5mg is the standard active ingredient in most widely available commercial emergency contraceptive pills. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h4)

question: How does ulipristal acetate differ from standard levonorgestrel emergency pills regarding timing?

options.A: It must be taken within the first 12 hours to have any effect
options.B: It requires a dual-dose schedule spaced exactly 24 hours apart
options.C: It is only effective if taken before the onset of menses
options.D: It remains effective up to 120 hours with sustained efficacy late in the window

explanation: Ulipristal acetate is a selective progesterone receptor modulator that maintains better efficacy up to 5 days post-intercourse than levonorgestrel. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h4)

question: What is a major dual benefit of choosing the copper intrauterine device for emergency contraception?

options.A: It provides immediate emergency action and long-term ongoing contraception
options.B: It protects against sexually transmitted infections immediately
options.C: It cures pelvic inflammatory disease while preventing pregnancy
options.D: It completely eliminates menstrual bleeding for up to ten years

explanation: The copper IUD addresses the immediate risk of pregnancy and can then be left in place to provide years of continuous birth control. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h5)

question: How do copper ions primarily prevent pregnancy when the IUD is used as an emergency intervention?

options.A: By neutralizing vaginal pH to kill all bacteria instantly
options.B: By causing immediate atrophy of the entire myometrium
options.C: By impairing sperm motility and preventing fertilization
options.D: By completely stopping the pituitary gland from releasing FSH

explanation: Copper creates a spermicidal intrauterine environment that stops sperm from reaching and fertilizing an egg. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h5)

question: What is a crucial piece of history a nurse must obtain before administering emergency contraception?

options.A: The results of a mandatory cervical biopsy
options.B: The client's exact blood pressure baseline
options.C: A complete family history of cardiovascular disease
options.D: Exact time elapsed since unprotected intercourse

explanation: Knowing the precise hours elapsed since intercourse determines whether hormonal pills or an IUD will be effective. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h6)

question: Why is screening for the date of the last normal menstrual period essential during the pre-assessment?

options.A: To verify if the client is currently experiencing dysmenorrhea
options.B: To calculate the exact date of the client's next expected menopause
options.C: To determine the precise amount of iron replacement needed
options.D: To help evaluate if the client might already be pregnant from an earlier cycle

explanation: Emergency contraception is ineffective if a patient is already pregnant, making menstrual history vital to rule out pre-existing conception. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h6)

question: What action is typically required if a client vomits shortly after taking an oral emergency contraceptive pill?

options.A: No action is needed because absorption occurs instantaneously
options.B: The client should switch immediately to barrier methods for life
options.C: The client must undergo immediate surgical evacuation
options.D: The dose may need to be repeated due to incomplete absorption

explanation: Vomiting within a short window after ingestion means the medication may not have been fully absorbed into the system. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h7)

question: What instruction should a nurse give a client regarding her next expected menstrual period after taking emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: Expect potential alterations in timing, and test for pregnancy if menses is delayed over a week
options.B: Expect complete cessation of menses for the next three consecutive months
options.C: Expect heavy hemorrhage that requires emergency blood transfusion
options.D: Expect absolute regular timing matching her exact historical calendar day

explanation: Hormonal shifts often alter the next period's arrival date; a significant delay warrants ruling out treatment failure with a pregnancy test. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h7)

question: Which of the following is a common myth regarding emergency contraceptive pills in many communities?

options.A: They permanently alter eye color and vision
options.B: They cause permanent sterility in female users
options.C: They instantly cure all sexually transmitted infections
options.D: They guarantee immunity from future unplanned pregnancies

explanation: A widespread misconception is that emergency contraceptives permanently damage future fertility, which nurses must actively debunk. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h8)

question: What is an essential strategy for nurses in Nigeria to improve access to emergency contraception for young adults?

options.A: Requiring mandatory parental consent for all adult clients
options.B: Providing non-judgmental, confidential, and youth-friendly counseling services
options.C: Restricting access to married couples with verified fertility proof
options.D: Reporting all clients who request the pill to local community elders

explanation: Creating a welcoming and confidential environment reduces the fear of stigma and encourages timely help-seeking behavior among youth. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h8)
